chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them:
About a man who is behind an Imam, and he prolongs the tashahhud, then the urge to urinate comes upon him, or he fears that something will pass him by, or pain occurs to him—what should he do?
He said: “He gives the taslim, departs, and leaves the Imam.”

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the sitting testimony recited in the prayer
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: the urge or need to urinate
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: he gives the taslim ending the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a follower do if he needs to leave during a prolonged tashahhud in congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for someone praying behind an Imam who faces a pressing excuse during a prolonged tashahhud, such as the urge to urinate, fear of missing something important, or physical pain. Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام instructs that he should give taslim and leave, indicating concession in congregational prayer when hardship arises.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1192 - Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)
about a man who is behind an Imam and the Imam prolongs the tashahhud, causing the man to feel the urge to urinate, fear missing something, or experience pain. What should he do?
Imam (as) replied: "He should perform the taslim (salutation of peace), leave, and leave the Imam."
